Subject: Questions on DPA, subprocessor list & UK addendum

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team at BlueWave is excited about the latency numbers. Before we move further with procurement, our legal and privacy teams need a few items clarified:

- Full DPA that we can review (including standard data transfer mechanisms).
- Current subprocessors list and whether any subprocessors process data in the UK specifically.
- Do you offer the UK-specific addendum (IDTA / UK Addendum)? If yes, can you share a draft?
- Any completed TIAs / DTIA evidence for typical telemetry or customer uploads? We need a concise description of what data types are transferred and the safeguards applied.

We have a procurement cutoff end of month, so a quick turnaround would be ideal. Happy to set a short call if you prefer to walk through.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Bell
Head of Compliance, BlueWave Health

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Attaching our current DPA (v3) and the latest subprocessor export to this thread. A few quick notes:

- DPA_redwood_v3.pdf (attached) contains the standard SCCs for EU transfers embedded in Annex I and our controller/subprocessor roles clearly mapped.
- subprocessor_list_202703.csv (attached) shows data center locations; we flag which subprocessors have UK-hosted nodes in column "region".
- We do offer the UK addendum (IDTA / UK Addendum). Lauren (Legal) is looped in here and is preparing a draft tailored to regulated health data transfers.
- For TIAs/DTIAs: we have a templated TIA summary we can share that lists categories of data transferred (e.g., user-generated text, model telemetry, logs), retention expectations, and applied safeguards (encryption in transit/at rest, access controls, DLP screening). I can surface an example TIA summary as a short PDF within 24h.

Proposed next steps:
1) Lauren will send the UK addendum draft with the specific clause we use for UK government requirements.
2) I’ll follow up with a 1-page TIA summary and a short mapping of where customer-controlled PII would cross borders.
3) If that looks good, we can route the DPA/UK addendum to your procurement for a DocuSign flow.

If you’d like a brief call (20 min) to walk legal through the items, Karthik (our sales lead) can join to cover timelines and commercial impact.

Thanks — will send the TIA and addendum draft shortly.

—

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2027-03-18T14:35:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA, subprocessor list & UK addendum

Hi Sarah — pleased to meet you over email. I’m attaching a working draft of the UK Addendum (uk_addendum_draft_20270318.docx) for your review. A few items we’ve tried to address upfront based on common BlueWave requirements:

- Scope: clarifies processing of customer content for inference, telemetry for service health, and developer metadata.
- Cross-border controls: we include both SCCs (EU) and a UK-specific IDTA clause; we also provide an option for customers to require UK-only processing where Redwood Private is used (subject to capacity).
- Subprocessor transparency: we commit to 30-day notice for new subprocessors and provide an up-to-date export (see attached CSV).
- TIA/DTIA evidence: for regulated health customers we provide a TIA summary and an option for an in-person (or virtual) walkthrough with our security team. For now, please confirm the data classes you consider "sensitive patient data" vs. operational telemetry so we can annotate the TIA properly.

Questions for you to help us finalize:
1) Does BlueWave require a UK-data-residency guarantee for all processing or only for patient identifiers?
2) Is a signed IDTA required prior to any sandbox testing, or can we proceed under a standard DPA with a contractual commitment to execute the addendum before production?

I’ve left a few redlines in the draft for clause 4 (on transfers) and clause 9 (retention). If you can indicate a preferred timeline for review, we’ll prioritize the updates.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
Redwood Inference — Legal

Subject: Re: Questions on DPA, subprocessor list & UK addendum

Thanks Lauren and Jordan — this is exactly what we needed to start the internal review. A couple quick answers:

- BlueWave requires UK residency only for direct patient identifiers (name, NHS number, precise address). De-identified clinical notes and model interaction telemetry can be processed outside the UK provided strong pseudonymization.
- We prefer to sign the IDTA prior to production but can accept DPA + a commitment to execute the addendum before any live patient data is sent. Sandbox testing can proceed under the DPA if the addendum is in execution.

Next steps from our side: procurement will want the signed DPA and an idea of the commercial impact if we require UK-only processing for PHI. Can you send: (1) the TIA summary you mentioned, and (2) a short estimate (delta) on cost/timeline for enabling UK-only processing for patient identifiers?

If you can get the DocuSign link for the DPA when available, we’ll queue it for signature. Appreciate the quick turnaround — planning to escalate internally this afternoon.

Best,
Sarah
